chronology: [Prior recap] Don Nicanor dies; Steelhead excises his poet-self (Zaran Klezra) and defeats the Techno-Technos, nearly destroying Philodendra; he abducts the TechnoPope; bikramen draws galaxy-wide fleets; Steelhead sells Philodendra and relocates the Troglosocialists to a new artificial world.

[Prior recap] On the artificial world Dona Vicenta contracts tuberculosis and reveals she carries twins: a boy by Steelhead, a girl by Zaran. Only one can be delivered; Steelhead chooses the female child, fracturing the father-to-son succession rule.
[Flashback] Dona Vicenta lies gravely ill in the metasurgery, her body rejecting all treatments, her lungs inoperable. She despairs until reminded she still has her child.

[Flashback] The caesarean produces conjoined twins joined at the hip who share one brain; the girl's skull is hollow. Steelhead separates them surgically, transplants the shared brain into the girl, and reconstructs her skull.

[Flashback] Narration names the child Aghora—a being with a man's brain in a woman's body, described as 'deeper than deep.' A dying cyborg master linked to the beloved Klezea receives the newborn before succumbing to pulmonary hemorrhage.
[Flashback] Dona Vicenta is sealed in an omni-cryoshroud halting her biological processes and installed in the Hall of Weapons as a frozen maternal presence for Aghora's upbringing.

[Flashback] Steelhead assigns a genetically engineered tarantuwolf as Aghora's nursemaid; it nearly devours her repeatedly as an infant. By age five she has tamed it into a mount and rides it in live meteor-defense exercises around the metabunker.

[Flashback] At age seven Aghora undergoes the Metabaron slicer ordeal, submitting her left hand to progressive mutilation—fingers, hand, forearm—without crying out, and earns a bionic replacement hand.

[Flashback] Over subsequent years Aghora is implanted with Oko mini-bombs and internal weapons. She is assigned to the prison planet Khaliyuga, executing 200 condemned beings per day for three years—more than 200,000 kills total.
[Flashback] Aghora undergoes a gender-transformation rite, renouncing her feminine body; she is recognized as male by her father and begins a new initiation phase.
[Flashback] Grief over Dona Vicenta drives Steelhead to replace all his flesh, bones, and organs with Storlon flexible metal; he specifically removes his heart to erase emotional attachment.

[Flashback] On her sixteenth birthday Aghora faces the final initiation trial: a sword duel with Steelhead invoking Othon's ancestral code. They fight evenly for two days; on the third day Aghora's cut to Steelhead's waist has no effect—both combatants' metal bodies are proof against swords.

[Flashback] Aghora shatters Dona Vicenta's omni-cryoshroud pod with a sword strike, killing her preserved mother. She then defeats Steelhead with a freezing weapon, claims the title of new Metabaron, and has Steelhead launched into deep space.

[Aftermath] The new Metabaron (Aghora, female) waits three years for the Imperial Court to assign a mission. The robot narrators note that Steelhead's eventual return is expected and will produce the wound on the master's right eyebrow.

[Present] A mirror-fleet annihilates an imperial fleet and destroys the only planet in the Vurfni-Be system. An unidentified female observer notes the invasion of 'our universe' and wonders why she has not been summoned.

[Present] Aghora learns hostile forces are two weeks from the Golden Planet. She infiltrates its atmosphere using her Metashadow stealth craft with companion Deyanira and advances toward the glass dome as the issue ends.
locations: Metabunker — indestructible fortress in space, sacred sanctuary of the Metabaron, repository of Castaka secrets, residence of Tonto and Lothar
Metasurgery — advanced surgical chamber; site of Dona Vicenta's treatment and the twin birth and brain transplant
Hall of Weapons — chamber where Steelhead installs Dona Vicenta's omni-cryoshroud as an enduring maternal presence
Khaliyuga — prison planet receiving condemned beings from across the galaxy for execution
New artificial world — Troglosocialist relocation site after Philodendra's sale
Golden Planet — dwelling of the imperial couple; infiltrated by Aghora at the volume's end
Vurfni-Be system — site of the mirror-fleet battle; its only planet is destroyed
Outer space — where Steelhead is launched after his defeat by Aghora
lore_laws: Metabaron succession passes father to son; each son must kill his father to inherit the title.
The Castaka name can only be borne by sons per stated clan law.
Hyper-infrasound is a ranged weapon capable of destructive sonic discharge.
Omni-cryoshroud halts all biological processes, preserving a person in suspended near-death.
Tarantuwolf: a genetically engineered animal rated among the most dangerous in the galaxy.
Oko mini-bombs can be surgically implanted inside a living body.
Storlon is a flexible metal used to replace flesh, bone, and organs in full-body cybernetic conversion.
Khaliyuga is a galaxy-wide prison planet where condemned beings are sent for execution.
Krgptah (self-generating multi-lizard, Pengrix system) multiplies rather than dying when severed.
Metabunker: indestructible fortress, sacred sanctuary of the Metabaron, repository of Castaka secrets; residence of Tonto and Lothar.
Metashadow: stealth craft or concealment system capable of bypassing planetary detection.
The Imperial Court controls mission assignments for the Metabaron.
Mirror-ships can replicate and destroy an opposing fleet by confronting it with its own reflection.
The Golden Planet is the dwelling of the imperial couple.
Ganya is an intoxicant capable of impairing a warrior's control.
A being with a man's brain in a woman's body is designated Aghora in narration.
major_events: Steelhead chooses the female twin over the male heir, fracturing the father-to-son Metabaron succession rule and setting the entire volume's premise.
Surgical birth: conjoined twins with one shared brain are separated; the brain is transplanted into the girl, who is named Aghora, establishing her dual-gendered identity.
Dona Vicenta sealed in omni-cryoshroud and enshrined in the Hall of Weapons as a frozen maternal icon over Aghora's childhood.
Aghora tames the tarantuwolf nursemaid by age five; completes the age-seven slicer ordeal, losing her left hand to earn a bionic replacement.
Aghora weaponized with Oko mini-bombs and internal weapons; deployed to Khaliyuga, executing more than 200,000 prisoners over three years.
Aghora undergoes gender-transformation rite, renouncing her feminine body and beginning a new initiation phase.
Steelhead replaces his entire body with Storlon metal and removes his own heart to extinguish grief over Dona Vicenta.
Three-day initiation sword duel between Aghora and Steelhead; sword combat fails against both metal bodies.
Aghora destroys Dona Vicenta's preservation pod, killing her mother, as the decisive act of the duel.
Aghora defeats Steelhead with a freezing weapon, claims title of new Metabaron; Steelhead is launched into deep space.
Mirror-fleet invasion destroys an imperial fleet and the sole planet of the Vurfni-Be system.
Aghora infiltrates the Golden Planet via Metashadow with Deyanira, moving toward the glass dome.
open_uncertainties: Whether Aghora biologically sired the current no-name Metabaron is disputed in-story: one account asserts it, another proposes the child was conceived by another Steelhead.
The precise circumstances of the master's right-eyebrow scar are linked to Steelhead's expected future return for revenge but are not yet depicted.
Deyanira's exact nature—living creature, biomechanical mount, or other companion—is not defined by the end of the volume.
The origin, mechanism, and goal of the mirror-fleet invasion remain unexplained; the volume ends before Aghora reaches the glass dome.
The fate of the boy twin after the brain transplant is not shown.
The identity of the dying cyborg master who receives baby Aghora (invoking 'my beloved Klezea') is not confirmed by name in the page summaries.
Whether the succession dispute over Aghora's legitimacy as a Castaka heir is ever formally resolved within the lineage is left open.
recurring_motifs: Extreme bodily mutilation as rite of passage and proof of Castaka worthiness (slicer ordeal, amputation, organ replacement, brain transplant)
Father-to-child succession repeatedly subverted or complicated by gender and biology
Love and emotional attachment framed as fatal warrior weakness, ritually or surgically excised
Full cybernetic body replacement as response to grief and desire for invulnerability
Robot narrators recounting lineage history as a bickering oral-archive framing device
Preservation technology (omni-cryoshroud, stasis pod) suspending people between life and death
Pain endurance as the core measure of Castaka identity
Mirror or reflected identity: twins sharing one brain; a fleet destroyed by its own mirror-duplicate
title: Aghora, The Father-Mother
